utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-04-75-T, The Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer; Sarah Clanton; Case Manager, Thomas Laugel; and legal interns, Moritz von Normann and Sarah Munsch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzic, I would like to ask you a little even though you already said a few things about this, but in any case, I wanted to ask you about the Vance Plan. If you can just briefly tell us how the events followed one another and what were your positions with regard to the Vance Plan, from the negotiations stage to the stage when it was concluded.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As early as in late fall 1991, specific talks began about the arrival of the UN peace forces. We have already talked about the contacts I had with representatives of the European community, Mr. Wijnaendts and Ahrens, and after that we established contact with Mr. Goulding. I believe that he was an envoy of the Secretary-General, and with Cyrus Vance. There were many problems because we were concerned for the security of the population. Our goal, at least the goal of the government and mine, and I was heading the government, was to achieve peace and to end the killing. It's well-known that we had a series of meetings and consultations, all of them held in Belgrade with federal representatives or with mediators from the UN, and before that, the European community, as I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was the general position of the Croatian Serbs towards the proposals contained in the Vance Plan initially?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Vance Plan generally said that the peacekeeping forces would be coming to Croatia. This was a problem for us, and I mentioned a referendum that we had held and the decisions of the assembly which I had to implement, I mean my assembly, and we believed that instead of Croatia the notion of Yugoslavia or a part of Yugoslavia should be used or something like that. Perhaps it was a rather formal problem but for us it was a practical one too. And then Mr. Vance promised to us that Croatia would be treated as a geographical notion without envisaging any final political solution, and that satisfied more than 50 per cent of my requests. When I say "my," I mean the requests of the government that I was representing. The government of SAO Krajina which was headed by Milan Babic was much tougher in its stance. It had greater demands and problems arose because of this. Once again, I say that our position was that the Blue Helmets would come to the demarcation line, that they should guarantee that the Croatian forces would not be able to enter and threaten us. It's known that they did come and that they were deployed throughout the territory. So these were the issues that we needed to agree about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what were the views with regard to the deployment of the UN forces in the territory of both SBWS and the SAO Krajina before that, in terms of the places where these force were supposed to be deployed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I just said, our view was that they should be deployed along the demarcation line, the confrontation line, and according to plan, they were supposed to be deployed throughout the territory and they were to be in charge of the security of all the population, including the population inside the territory. Very soon, it turned out that this was bad because they did not then keep the border, nor the depth of the territory, so this was a half-baked solution, but I didn't really know it at that time. It just turned out to be like that later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see please P28. It is tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the minutes from one of the meetings of the SFRY Presidency attended by a number of representatives of SBWS and the Knin Krajina. I see that you were among them. Do you remember -- or, rather, I will ask you to look at page 37 in the original and in translation it's pages 27 and 28. Have you refreshed your memory?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether your words are truly conveyed here.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Inter alia, what you say here is: "I have to say what the position of our people and our assembly is. The people believe that the suffering should stop." It's on page 39. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also say that you advocate the deployment along the green line. What was the green line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The so-called green line was the separation line, the confrontation line, or the demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see now P29. It is tab number 16, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another meeting and the occasion is the same. It was held on the 12th of December at 1330 hours. I see that your name is not included among those present. Could you tell us what was the reason for your absence from this meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can see that Babic is not there either. I don't know why we were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see on pages 32 and 33 of the original - pages 24, 25 in English version - that Milosevic is asking the question why you and Babic did not attend, and he says: "Could anyone have any more urgent business than attending the meeting?" Can you remember any reasons why you were not there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there I remember in a way our conflict with Milosevic began then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what did the conflict consist of for you? What was your grudge against Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have much choice at the time. I had to take into account the positions of the assembly and the referendum and the positions of the SAO Krajina. They were more numerous and that was a greater territory than the SBWS. So I showed solidarity in a way with the positions that I considered rational as long as I did. Once I thought that they were no longer rational, then I, of course, defended only the position of the government I was heading and the territory in which I was at the time. Both Babic and I believed that Milosevic wanted to resolve this issue quickly and at any cost, in such a way that our requests wouldn't be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After the adoption of the Vance Plan, you gave an interview to the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we see document -- it is tab 1363. It is actually the document 885 from the Prosecution Rule 65 terlist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's an interview you gave on the 18th -- or, rather, it was published on the 18th and the 19th of January, 1992. In it, you say, "We have been cheated." Can you remember -- or, rather, you can remind yourself from the text, why did you feel cheated at the time and who cheated you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not in accordance what we had been arranging with Mr. Vance when the plan was being adopted and also the guarantees provided by our federal state and the Republic of Serbia which was one of the participants and stakeholders in the negotiations. From my present point of view, I think it was very brave and it was the strange and -- criticism of Milosevic the most stringent that was possible at the time. I'm not sure how I dare to do it at the time, but it was the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D139, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I have just been informed this document was not on the Defence's list for use during the direct. It is among those that fall within the pending motion to amend his 65 ter list from the 1st of July. So I just wish to note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, the Prosecution did not object to this motion. And, as far as I recall, the Chamber decided about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I wouldn't know on the top of my head, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't know either, Mr. President, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll look into it, Mr. Stringer, Mr. Zivanovic. Yeah, we keep it as it is for the moment and we'll come back to you. Please continue, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, before the adoption of the plan, you had a meeting with Mr. Goulding. I would now ask you to look at the document P32, which is tab 19. Do you remember this conversation? Did you agree all these items from this report with Mr. Goulding or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those were the views that we advocated as listed here by Mr. Goulding from (a) to (f). And in particular, there was the position on disarming that was emphasised because they requested that only one side should be disarmed, and Croatia was free to arm itself on the other hand and it was not disarmed literally 1 or 200 metres from this green line, and they could choose and attack any point along the border with us whenever they wanted to. And later on it really turned out that that was so, without any consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did Mr. Goulding give you the answers that are noted here in this letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he said that. After his assurances, I said that I would accept the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this item (c) of his response, is that correctly phrased as well?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't understand him saying that, but -- which item did you say again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought you said (e) but you're thinking of (c). Yes, this is correctly formulated and defined, and that was one of the main reasons we accepted the plan. Because with the withdrawal of the JNA, which was responsible for the territory and had the control of the territory, they handed over that control to the United Nations over a period of a month or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just for the purpose of clarification, we're now speaking about the response of Mr. Goulding. So it's on page 2, both of the English and the B/C/S text. I am just saying this for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph (c) from this response, was that implemented at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it was not. UNPROFOR did not manage to protect the line of separation. We had to do that ourselves. We had to mobilise the population from the interior of the area and then there was nobody to keep law and order and make sure that the citizens were secure, and UNPROFOR didn't do that either. So this was a very difficult thing to put into effect for our local leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at these stenographic minutes from the meeting of the Presidency of the 2nd of March, 1992. This is P37, tab 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The session was held on the 2nd of March, 1992. I would like us to clarify something that you said then. This is on page 92 of the original and on page 68 of the English translation. The text actually begins from page 88 of the B/C/S and page 66 in the English translation. And the resettlement of the population from one territory to another was discussed. Radovan Karadzic spoke about this. When you addressed the meeting, after he said that it was just ridiculous for people to move from one area to another, on page 92 of the B/C/S and page 68 of the English translation, you said that this was not a nebulous thing.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you said Serbs from Zagreb should resettle, as well as those from Belgrade, and now from this area; it's out of the question. So just allow me to clarify two matters here, even though what you said was very brief. Could you please tell us what you meant when you said that this is not a nebulous matter. There's nothing nebulous in it. This refers to the resettlement of the population?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not nebulous. It already happened. The Serbs had already moved from the bigger cities, either voluntarily or by being forced out. So it was not nebulous. Whereas Croats from Belgrade had no problems. They didn't have to move out and this is that difference. And I said that at this point in time, this is out of the question, not in this terrain. So this is an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the council.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said the following: The Serbs from Zagreb should resettle and Serbs from Belgrade, and now, as far as this terrain is concerned, this is out of the question. So there are two options here. It is evident that the way the sentence reads here doesn't make any sense. There are two options. I don't want to suggest either one to you because I think the way it is written is not accurate. I would like to see with you if you can clarify this.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first let me explain this. When I said this is not anything nebulous, these are my words. As for the rest of it, I was quoting the position of some people from the international community that Serbs from Zagreb should be resettled. That was normal. Nobody questioned that. It was implied -- and Serbs from Belgrade. But nobody talked about Croats. Had Croats been discussed then it would have been a crime, but as for Serbs nobody was interested. This is what I meant. And then what I meant was at this point in time that is out of the question. That is what I meant to say. The way it's written here, it doesn't make sense. It's nebulous.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the sense of the sentence was when you say: "Serbs from Zagreb and Serbs from Belgrade should resettle but at this point in time, this is out of the question." Why was it out of the question at that particular moment but yesterday it was possible as well as the following day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the position in the field and as far as international policy was concerned. Serbs were being resettled or were resettling, and this was not a problem for anyone. And at that point in time, nobody would have listened to us. That's the sense of it. There -- there was -- it was out of the question for us to talk about this problem with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D3292, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is tab 1147.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report about talks conducted and, among other people, you were also present.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 3. Actually, page 4, please. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In item 8, it states here: [In English] "Hadzic, the so-called president of Serbian Krajina, expressed surprise at my proposal, saying that he did not expect pre-judgement of political decisions by the United Nations. He said there are two options before the 50.000 Serbs living in the pink zones: To be assured of protection, or to leave." [Interpretation] Do you remember that meeting that you had with international representatives on the topic of the pink zones and other matters discussed in this matter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. The term "pink zones" had to do with the SAO Krajina because in the SBWS there were no pink zones. The whole area was a so-called blue area, under the United Nations. Pink zones were in the western Krajina in areas populated by Serbs with Serb authority and where the United Nations did not want to go there. They were not supposed to be part of the UNPA zones, and I said that there were only two options here: Either to provide protection for those people or they would have to leave. Because once the Croatian authorities arrived, they would not be assured of safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember what happened to the pink zones after this? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pink zones were periodically attacked and then taken over by the Croat forces without any consequences for them in relation to the international community. There were killings. The area was occupied. And, as far as I know, no one has so far been charged with that, either in Croatia or here. This question was never considered by any court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened to the population in the pink zones? You said, among other things, that some were killed. What happened to those who were not killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were expelled. They were second-class refugees. Nobody really considered their status.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where those refugees went, as you said, after they were expelled?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them came to the territory under the control of the Serbian Krajina. Perhaps some went to Serbia and Bosnia. I don't know that, but it was not a very large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, I wanted to get an explanation from you about setting up the military authority, particularly in the area of SBWS in 1991. Yesterday, you said that on the 20th of November you received notification from Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic that the civilian authority cannot be saved or spared and that, actually, it cannot be set up and that for a long time afterwards it could not be set up in Vukovar. So I just briefly wanted to look at documents on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see please P1994.1981. It is tab number 1284.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just before paragraph 4, there is a paragraph that said that: "The town commanders in the OG JUG area of responsibility are to take all necessary measures for the full functioning of the military authorities pursuant to the order of the 9th of November." Does this correspond to what you know and what you talked about, about the setting up of the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just add about Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic. Not only did he say that it was not possible to set up civilian authorities but it was not even to be discussed. He was not prepared to even discuss that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see now D20, please. It is tab number 1226.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at paragraph 2 of this order which is dated 22nd November, 1991. It says that: "The staff of the Territorial Defence of Vukovar, in co-operation with the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade, will establish organs of authority in local communes and organise their functioning, set up police station, regulate the movement of people returning to town and their compulsory identification of the Velepromet reception centre." Do you remember, was this done?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is completely consistent with the actual situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see now P169 -- oh, sorry. P1996.1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another order from the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade dated 22nd November, 1991. Would you just look at this sentence above paragraph 3: "Prevent any form of harassment of the population and local residents, as well as unauthorised entry and search of flats and houses."

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this consistent with what you knew in that period; namely, that this order existed and that your authorities, the authorities of SBWS, were supposed to informs -- this.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were not able to do these things even before. This order just confirms the actual situation. We didn't even have access to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P200 -- sorry.P2000.1981, tab 86.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report dated 29 November, 1991. Among other things, it says that following the liberation of Vukovar the command of the brigade operating as the Town Command got the task of enforcing the powers of the military authority -- military administration. Do you know if therewas a military administration at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at 2007.1987 [as interpreted], tab 447.[In English] 2007.1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see this order dated 30th December, 1991, where the TO Staff of Vukovar is resubordinated to the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade which is, at the same time, the Town Command?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 3, this unit is given the order to start disarming Chetnik groups in populated areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move to the next page. Only in the original. The English text is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5: The staff of the TO Vukovar is responsible for the population and their property and in carrying out this task, the staff is relying on the units of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Does this reflect the situation in Vukovar at that time, as far as you and the government knew?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everything was under military rule; that is to say, under this 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see please P376. It is tab 1256.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a regular combat report dated 18 January, 1992, again from the Command of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Could you please look at paragraph 2. It says: "The staff of the Territorial Defence ofVukovar is not functioning at all and its organisational structure has not been established either." Nobody knows how many units there are or who are the commanders or commanding officers, and they don't have any communications. Did you or the government have any contacts with the TO Staff Vukovar? Did you have any jurisdiction over them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P151, tab 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision that you signed that the government passed on the 21st of January, 1992. Let's begin with paragraph 2. It says: "The Command of the 1st Army District is given the authority to enforce paragraph 1." Namely, to disband the unit led by a man known as Kameni and based in Vukovar. Can you remember how this decision came to be adopted and how did you come to sign it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there was a session of the government where Colonel Ristic came and said it would be a first step in the transition from the military to civilian rule, and it would be good for us to adopt this decision, the text of which he had already written, and the secretary of the government was only supposed to add this heading. We discussed it and accepted it. And he explained that it would be a good idea for our local police, because they know most of the members of Kameni's units, to help, to avoid casualties. But I didn't get any follow-up information, whether this was really done, or how.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you said "Colonel Ristic," you meant Colonel Ratko Ristic, a JNA colonel?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see his name is Ratko now. I just knew his last name, Ristic. He was a JNA colonel from the Novi Sad Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- in fact, did the government know the identity of this person mentioned in paragraph 1 at that time because he is cited only by nickname?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood, it was some kind of detachment commanded by a person under that nickname. I didn't know him, but I'd heard of him, and I knew he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party. But I didn't know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you knew only his nickname. You didn't know his first or last name. I'm asking you because only the nickname is given here. It's just said this unit is led by so-called Kameni. I'm only asking if you remember.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's obvious that at that time we didn't know. I later found out the man is called Milan Lancuzanin. But I didn't know it at the time. We knew his nickname, Kameni. I found out later from media reports that it's Milan Lancuzanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1, reference is made to some plan and programme of activities to implement tasks related to the establishment of civilian authorities in the territory of Vukovar municipality. What kind of plan and programme was it? Did you see it? Did you participate in its creation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, and I don't believe anyone in our government did. If that thing existed, I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After this, did Colonel Ristic or anyone else inform you if this decision was ever realised? Was anything really done? Were any steps taken?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody gave any follow-up information to me or anyone in the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at D50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tab 1238. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is an order dated 17 February, 1992, whereby the Command of the 1st Military District is issuing certain orders regarding civilian affairs, and I would like us to look at paragraph 2. I believe it's on the second page of the English. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This shows that this was complete military rule. They appointed town commanders and all the other organs. They were able to replace them as they pleased. And it was all done back in February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "they," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, an order is given to protect loyal citizens of Croatian, Hungarian, and other nationalities from terror, liquidation, and all kinds of pressure. Are you able to tell us how you understood this? But, first of all, tell me if you were aware of this order, because it relates to civilian affairs.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware because they did not inform the government about it. I knew that it was their obligation, as it was their zone of responsibility, to take care of all affairs, including the civilian ones. But the way it's formulated doesn't seem logical to me because, to me, all the citizens were equal. I don't know what was the discretion on the basis of which one was supposed to decide whether they were loyal or unloyal. For me, whoever continued to live with us was a loyal citizen. In my view, this allows the possibility of manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see please 1D365. It is tab number 749.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a statement by Colonel Vojnovic which he gave on the 29th of November, 1991, in which he says that the main task of the military authorities which have been established was to help in setting up the civilian authorities. I'm interested in this: Since your talks with Colonel Vojnovic on the 20th of November at Velepromet and onwards, were you personally or the government in contact with him in order to establish civilian authorities through the government of SBWS, as we have already seen how the civilian authorities were set up through the Vukovar TO Staff?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any contact with him, neither myself nor the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tendered this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, 1D2493. It is tab 1062.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now move to something else somewhat further afield from Vukovar. This is a document from January 1992 on the appointment of a director of an enterprise there. Do you know whether the government was consulted, for example, about the appointment not only of this director but directors of other enterprises which had nothing to do with military affairs? We are talking about Ilok at the moment.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government was not consulted about such issues in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we -- I would tendered this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D141.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P379.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tab number 1259.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another report about the setting up of TO Staffs in the territory of Ilok. It was submitted on the 26th of February, 1992, and it provides details -- a detailed analysis of all this. Could you please say whether your government, the government of SBWS, took part in the setting up of units and staffs of Territorial Defence in the territory of Ilok and its surroundings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, 3187. P3187. It is tab 1331.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another document from the Command of the 1st Motorised Corps dated the 20th of March, 1992, and it has to do with the action of populating the territory of Krajina. It is requested that all the officers be informed about the possibilities and conditions of populating the territory of Krajina and that information about those who may be interested be urgently submitted. Do you know whether people did, indeed, become settled in accordance with this order of the JNA, and were there any consultations with your government?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a period when the Republic of Serbian Krajina had already been formed, and no one was consulted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that this is the period after you had been elected to the position of the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I'm interested in the previous period. Did they consult the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem? So my question does not refer to the government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody consulted the government of SBWS while I was the prime minister. Not about this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see please P1692.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Tab number 1270.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just looked at some documents dealing with Vukovar and the surrounding area. I would now like us to look at some other documents that also have to do with the setting up of the military authorities in the same time-frame but in the zone of the 12th Corps. This is why I'd like you to look at this document. First of all, in this document dated the 22nd of November, 1991, it says that the groups and units which are not under the command of the JNA had to be removed. From what you know, was this an ongoing JNA's task after the fall of Vukovar in the area; namely, to have the territory under control and all army forces and armed groups that there were?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that after the fall of Vukovar, in accordance with the orders of the commander of the 1st Military District which I could hear in the media, only the JNA and the forces that were under its command were allowed to be in the territory. Whoever was outside their command was to be expelled across the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 reads that: "The command of the 12th Corps has the information that certain officers take it upon themselves to pass judgement on prisoners on the spot, which is impermissible." I'd like to know whether the government ever received any warnings that some of its members or organs were doing anything like this.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the government were not doing anything like this and I'm not even aware of this. I'm not familiar with this order. I saw for the first time here that something like that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to remind you of my question: Did the government ever receive any information about the military authorities to the effect that they had information that some people who were under civilian control or, let's say, government employees or the employees of local authorities did anything like this, as described under item 3?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we never received that sort of information from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we please see P2972.2913. It is tab 1319. Number is P2972.2913, and tab number 1319.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document about a tour that a team from the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade conducted in its zone of responsibility on the 7th of December, 1991. It says that volunteer units are integrated in the JNA and under its command with the exception of one unit from the 24th -- I don't really understand this abbreviation. My impression is that it's some artillery unit. And a TO Crnogorac detachment, which is reportedly under the control of the government of Serbia. Do you know that at the time there were any other units that were not under the control of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to go back to Ilok for yet a while, and if we could please see 2746. It's tab 619.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the Command of the 1st Infantry Guards Motorised Division which orders the setting up of military authorities in Ilok and places to the south of it, in that area. The units which are to discharge these duties are appointed. Please tell me whether you know that military rule was introduced in these places as stated in this report, in this order?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that military rule was introduced. The people were appointed by the army. It wasn't our civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see please D30. It is tab 1232.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a letter which you wrote to the commander of Ilok. You can see your signature on the following page. Do you remember this letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the letter, among other things, you say that you were not informed about the terms under which military authority was introduced. What did you want to explain by that? What did you actually want to say in this letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said, that nobody notified us about any conditions of the military authority: Under which conditions it was set up, what was the purpose of it, how long it would last.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Among other things, you said that Vojin Susa was assigned as the government representative to liaise with the JNA organs, particularly regarding the setting up of civilian authority. Could you please tell us what specific tasks did Mr. Susa receive from the civilian government.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the tragic events in Western Slavonia and after the refugees arrived in a disorganised manner to Eastern Slavonia, after we were informed about this and with a delay of about a month or so, the government formed a commission headed by Vojin Susa, who was supposed to base himself in Ilok and help as much as possible to organise things. I think that this was in late 1991. We asked that -- the military authorities to co-operate, if possible, there, to find them accommodation and things like that because we didn't have any powers in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also asked that the finance minister be given an overview of the situation in Ilok. What was meant by that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you remember, yesterday I said that the military authorities completely sealed off Ilok and the area around it, that they took over all the private companies, all the goods, and we had no overview. So we wanted the finance ministry to be able to look into the funds, the invoices, the number of supplies in Ilok, but our request was not granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we can move to the next page.Page 3 in the English text.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said, among other things, that you wanted some information about the Ilok police station because you said that you didn't know whether it was under military police. Could you please tell me if you had civilian police in Ilokat all at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I asked the Ilok town commander about the police. We knew that there was some sort of police force there, but we didn't know who set it up and who was in control and command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the letter, you said that the government had been told that the process of repopulation went on -- went on rather well. Did you have any information in the meantime that people were moving in to Ilok and who organised and led this whole operation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had information that this was managed by the military administration. They didn't ask for our approval in that, nor did they need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that you were not even aware of the criteria for this repopulating.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what this letter -- in your letter where you say: Our agreement is not required.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that directly. I believe that it was implied that we were not asked for our opinion, and that's what I said. This means that we were not responsible for anything. Nothing was in our jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were not required to give your approval for the things that they had already done?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that they did, they did of their own accord. They didn't ask us about anything, and they didn't think that they needed to do that. And this is precisely why I wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vojin Susa conveyed the town commander's request to give an approval for the temporary resettlement in the area of Ilok. Are you -- do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they told Susa that we didn't do anything about that, that they criticised him, and that they asked us about it ultimately, but I don't remember anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question on this document. In this document, you noted that with the resettlement you had no intention of prejudging the solution of military issues in Western Slavonia. Could you please explain what you meant to say about that in the document.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is easy to explain. When I say that the government had exclusively humanitarian goals, we did not interfere or get involved in any ethnic matters. These people found themselves on the Danube, on the border. They had no houses and they simply occupied or moved into those houses. We considered this to be a temporary move. Whether it would be a year or less, or longer, this is something that we did not deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it is time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before taking the break, I would like to try to settle the problem about document number 885 on the OTP Rule 65 ter list, the document we admitted as D139. It seems -- as far as we could check, Mr. Zivanovic, it seems that this document is not part of one of your motions to add documents to the -- to your 65 ter list. There's one of those motions, I think, still pending for which the OTP answer is due today, but this document is not on that list. If you could please check and in -- in the -- during the break. And in the meantime, the OTP could perhaps say whether they -- what their position is with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We don't have an objection, Mr. President, to the document. We can -- if the Chamber is minded to allow it to be added to the list, we don't object to it's being then tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If -- the document will be added to the 65 ter list and stays admitted and marked, as it is. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzic, do you remember receiving an answer from the Ilok town commander to this letter which we were discussing just before the break?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P1962. It is tab 468.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzic, did you find one answer at least to the questions that you put in the letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P369. It is tab 250.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a letter, or a telegram, sent by the Command of the 1st Guards Division to the Command of the 1st Military District requesting instructions about what to do about the resettlement and how to bring back members of other ethnic groups to the area and also to get people who left the area to return. Did you know that the military authorities at the time had dilemmas that are stated here in paragraphs 1 and 4 of the letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you consulted about your position on these issues on which they were seeking instructions from their superior command?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not consulted. No one asked me anything about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P370.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's tab number 251.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the answer that was received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we see the next page, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This answer of the 23rd of December, 1991, mentions -- or, rather, certain instructions are provided and the letter, among other things, says that: "The questions put should be most closely connected to the requests of Serbs from other areas to move into abandoned houses." Could you please tell me, were you aware of this position of the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that the leasing of abandoned houses should be left to the extent possible to the civilian authorities, wherever they exist, and if they don't exist, the Town Command should seek the opinion of the commissioner for Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and if there is no commissioner, then they should seek the opinion of the government. I want to know did anyone approach the government of the SBWS after these instructions were issued?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if any commissioners appointed by the government were asked for their opinion?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, the government did not appoint any commissioners, and I don't know how you would call this group that included Vojo Susa. In any case, they were formed after this letter. I don't know. I don't have any information that anyone was consulted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Hadzic, I -- Mr. Hadzic, I noticed that you stopping paying attention to the little cross on the screen that indicates when interpretation -- has finished interpreting the question. It is very helpful if you could do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, it says that no matter who makes the decision for people to move in, their houses that were abandoned by people who are certain not to return because of the crimes they had committed should be the first on the list to be given, to be made available. Were you aware of this? Were you informed about this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that it's natural that efforts should be made in co-operation with the authorities to enable the return of persons who had been loyal and who had not comprised themselves in any way. Were you informed of this position?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Further below, we read that all cases of illegal eviction should be registered and resolved in co-operation with the security organs of the JNA and the public security authorities of the district and towns. Did the government know that the military security and the public security were instructed to proceed in this way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody informed us about the activities of the military security or the public security, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the end, it says that Town Commands are especially responsible for securing law and order, the security and safety of citizens. Any harassment and mistreatment of citizens must not be allowed and the authorities are to prevent any such incidents. As far as you knew, were the Town Commands responsible for this, and did they really enforce it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Town Commands were responsible, and they were supposed to enforce it, but I did not get any reports whether they really did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P2750, tab 623.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report that the Command of the 1st Guards Division sent out covering capacities for accommodating refugees. It relates to Ilok and the surrounding area. I see here that they provide a specific number of housing units available to refugees. Did the government have an exact list of housing units available at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't know that. And the government did not deal with these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe we should move to the next page in English. It says, among other things, that it was on the 19th of December, 1991, that the refugees began to receive accommodation and the person who authored this report says that it would be natural for some ministry of the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem to form a subcommittee for immigration, a regional council for resettlement, and in populated areas, there should be commissions, and that it would be natural for the government to have exact data, to monitor convoys, make lists of requirements, collect lists of registered housing in order to implement the provision of accommodation and the resettlement of population. How would you comment on this report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that follows very clearly from this report. I'm not really interested in what a JNA officer considers natural, but we see from this report that the government did not deal with any of these matters that he criticises us over. We did not have these commissions, and we did not effect resettlement the way this officer would have wanted us to do. All this simply took us by surprise as a whirlwind, and we did not organise a resettlement in any planned way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify this, because I don't think the explanation on the record is very clear. You used two terms: "Moving out" and "moving in," or "evacuation" and "immigration."

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "resettlement," I meant the problem of refugees from Western Slavonia. That literally befell us unexpectedly. We could never have anticipated it. And when I said "moving out," or "evacuation," we didn't either plan it or implement it in any way. And from the critique addressed to us by this officer, it is clear that what I just explained is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My next question would be then: Why didn't you? What was in your way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the territory was under the control of the Yugoslav People's Army. We did not have civilian authorities in order to be able to implement this, or to enforce it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P3178. That's tab 716.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from the Chief of Staff of the 1st Military District sent to the 1st Mechanised Corps and the 12th Corps, and it says that you, the prime minister of the Serbian District of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, approached their command asking for property, vehicles and such, to be returned in order to be made available to the Serbian district. Can you tell me how you approached the Command of the 1st Military District, considering that we don't have your original letter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we addressed this military command in Ilok several times with regard to these problems, but we never received an answer to our previous requests, and then we tried this way. But this didn't bring about any solutions either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that there are two different matters here: Vehicles that had belonged to enemy units; and vehicles that the JNA had unlawfully seized from civilians and others. What was all this about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's a qualification they made. We asked to see what happened with various vehicles that had been seized from agricultural organisations, from the winery and its director, various other officials, because we were supposed to reappoint these officials, and they were supposed to have cars, and the cars had been seized by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P3179. It is tab 717.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see from this letter that later the 1st Motorised Corps addressed the same request to a whole series of units under its command. I am curious: Did you ever receive an answer from any of these units or from this corps or from the 1st Military District?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P2943. It is tab 658.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an instruction on conducting civilian affairs sent by the Federal Secretariat for National Defence to JNA units on 25 November, 1991. I want to review it briefly and then ask you a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move on to page 4, item 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 6 of this instruction, it is said that the civilian affairs organs are to undertake and carry out certain investigative actions and press criminal charges against the perpetrators of criminal acts. Were you informed that this was part of their jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not informed about the document that I am looking at now, but I did know that this was their jurisdiction, and only theirs. It couldn't have been anyone else's.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move to page 5, item 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Here it also reads that they're responsible for conducting administrative duties with regard to procurement, holding and carrying weapons and ammunition and issues approvals in that regard. Did you know that this was also their exclusive jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have a look at item 18. It's the following page in B/C/S and in English. I think that it's still on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says there that in the civilian affairs organs, the commands of places are to take measures, both preventive and repressive, to present sabotage activities, the spreading of defeatism, and so on. Did you know that this was also within their jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know all the details, but generally I did know this, because it was a jurisdiction within the JNA's zone of responsibility and also the military administration's jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please look at page 9, item 8. I think that it is on page 9. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The last sentence of item 8 reads that the order of superior commanders, should the execution of it not constitute a criminal act, is legally binding. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And another thing, Mr. Hadzic, as this document often mentions co-operation with civilian authorities, I'm interested in knowing whether you or the government were familiarised with the contents in any way whatsoever, not just by receiving such military instructions but verbally or in writing or in any way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not informed about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P3163. It is tab number 714.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, this document is under seal. We are not broadcasting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it should not be broadcasted. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a document about talks held on 8 April, 1992, between representatives of the international community and General Pujic, who is the author of the previous document that we looked at. Let us not quote the whole document because it's quite long. They complained a lot about the situation and the lack of protection of the civilians in the SBWS territory, and they addressed him. In view of the date, the 7th of April, 1992, I'd like to know whether you think that it was precisely the JNA, the Federal Secretariat of National Defence, that was the correct address where they ought to have raised this issue and who was able to resolve such an issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what were the responsibilities that the JNA had in April 1992 with regard to protecting the population in the SBWS territory.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the JNA had the sole responsibility. It was on the side which had signed the Vance Plan. The Serbs and their leadership in Slavonia and Baranja only accepted it, but those who signed it and took on themselves the obligation to implement it were the federal state on the one hand and the Republic of Croatia on the other. So that those who had come from the UN knew who was responsible and who they should address.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will read out to you one paragraph from page 3 of this document. Or, rather, I won't read it out to you but I will just summarise it so that we wouldn't take up too much time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have P2751. It's tab 624.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is another order from the Command of the 1st Military District dated the 7th of January, 1992. I will ask you to focus on item 2, which reads that: "The Town Commands of BeliManastir, Vukovar, Dalj, Osijek, based in Tenja and Vinkovci, based in Mirkovci, shall be responsible for carrying out civil affairs throughout the territory of the municipality in whose centre they are located." Please tell me whether the civil affairs organs were responsible for carrying out civil affairs throughout the municipalities where they were located.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, obviously it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And other and than these municipalities, was there any other territory in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was 100 per cent coverage of SBWS of the five municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, P1717.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Sorry. Tab number 385.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an order by the Command of the 1st Mechanised Corps of the 18th of February, 1992, and it's an analysis of the work of Military Districts. It also appoints a commission and other matters. I would like to ask you to look at item 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is on page 3 of the English translation of the document and on page 2 of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The order here is to "examine the work of the local commanders and authorities in the rural local communes." The order also states that, "All comprised officials are to be removed and that -- tested and trusted people ought to be appointed." Are you able to tell us how you understand this point on appointing tested and trusted people?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand it just as it's written, but also according to the situation in the field, and that meant tested and trusted people from the perspective of the Yugoslav People's Army and its policies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4 here which talks about the protection from threats of liquidation and terror of loyal non-Serb citizens, I think that we already discussed this on the basis of a different document which was issued by its superior command. What I'm interested here, however, is item 6, which orders that all measures should be taken in order to prevent paramilitary units from organising and from spending time in the area of responsibility. According to what you know about the situation in late February 1992, this attempt to prevent paramilitary units from forming, was that in the jurisdiction of the authorities?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was exclusively in the jurisdiction of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see document 2950, tab 661. Sorry, is it 2950?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. This is a 65 ter number or a --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, P.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: A P number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: A P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is another report from the Command of the 1st Mechanised Corps, dated 25th of February, 1992. In brief, the document states that the work of the Town Command and the president of the local commune has improved even though there are certain problems still.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page of English translation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And it says that the problems are expressed in the difficulties to elect organs of civilian authorities in the field and the -- their vetting. After that, it says that the election of those organs is in the jurisdiction of the Executive Board of the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and the municipalities, and that these are most often their people and that if the military authorities interfered in this, that would cause the dissatisfaction on the part of the government and the people. First of all, could you please tell us what this vetting was or verification of their suitability to be elected into the organs of civilian authority? Was this something that was done officially by the government, or was it an unofficial procedure?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of it officially. Nobody informed us about anything like that. As for the unofficial part, I already said that this was an official thing from the aspect of the policy of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And is this assertion correct that the election of these organs under the jurisdiction of the Executive Board of the SBWS -- are you aware that these Executive Boards or the government was responsible for the election of these organs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies that we discussed earlier were appointed by the army. Only once civilian authorities are set up, then the civilian authorities would be responsible once they assumed power. But what is not clear to me with this document is that the heading is the 25th of February, but the -- the document actually refers to the 27th of February, a couple of days later. So it's not clear to me how this exactly happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Defence counsel microphone was switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the first page. Can we first go back to the first page of the English text. Yes, what you mean to say is that the date of the letter, which is the answer to the request of the superior command, was written before the command actually requested it.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I noticed that because now suddenly the government is being talked about, whereas, the entire time they worked without any sort of agreement with the government or without any reference to it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, D37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is tab 1234.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You cannot really see the document very well, the original, but the translation is legible. Among other things, it is stated in the document that the local communes even -- that the local communes provided a list of persons whose safety is not being guaranteed. Can you please tell me, did you know about this? Do you know who drafted the list? At whose request? Why did the local communes make such lists and sends them to the army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about this. These local communes sent this to the army in a kind of personal way because these were local communes that were actually formed by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "local communes formed by the army," are you thinking of the local commune organs, the leadership of the local communes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm thinking of the leadership. Leadership that they referred to as being suitable. Suitable, as far as they were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see P1715. Sorry, it is tab 383.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a daily report of the organ for civilian affairs dated the 22nd of February about a meeting that was held the day before in Mirkovci. Attendees were mentioned, those who attended the meeting. I note that - and I'm asking you as well - whether anybody from the government, you or somebody else, did anybody attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from the government attended the meeting. I wasn't even informed about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In item 2, it is stated that the meeting was conducted by Major-General MicoDelic. I don't see him mentioned among those attending, but I don't doubt that that was so. I would like to know: Were you informed about the meeting later, or the results of the meeting? I'm not thinking only of you but of the government as a whole.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was not informed about it. Because after the 26th of February, I was no longer carrying out those duties. I don't think that the government was informed either, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at item 5, please. This is on the following page of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There are proposals here by the civilian affairs organ. Under article -- item 5 (a) which states: "Measures are to be taken at the level of the government of the Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja to quickly resolve the issue of settlement in areas that were hitherto unsettled, those being the villages of Nijemci, Apsevci, Podgradje, Lipovac, Slakovci, and to more effectively change the national makeup in places that are already settled." Were you and the government informed that a JNA organ put forward such a solution? Did you receive such a proposal from any JNA organ to this effect?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never received such a proposal, and so far I've never heard even that something like that existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We see under (b) another proposal from the same person: "For all displaced persons, regardless of their nationality, if they have participated in Ustasha units in any way, to be prohibited from returning to this area." Were you aware of such a proposal from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at item (d): "It is our opinion that Ceric village should be completely evacuated ..." Was this notified to you or the government?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither I nor the government were informed of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We'll look at one more document from this batch. P167, tab 126. It's a document authored by the same person only three days later sent directly to the Federal Secretary for National Defence, and if we look at item (b) -- I believe it's on page 3 in English. The text in English actually begins on page 2. The author lists major problems that make the work of civilian authorities difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we can now move to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Right at the beginning it says: "One of the problems is the emergence and existence of self-proclaimed governments and their ministers who arrogate the right to meddle in the work and organisation of civilian authorities." Looking at this reference to self-proclaimed governments, would you say that the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was called self-proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more than once. Both Serbia and Croatia and the international community labelled us that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, it is that time. Would that be convenient for you or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We can -- we can break now, Your Honours. I put this question after break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still have on the screen the same document. We should now move to page 2 of the original and the English remains on the same page. I'm interested in the first paragraph you see in the original, just before paragraph 2, referring to the intolerance between the Serbs who have moved in and the local Croats. It refers also to pressure exerted on people to move out and even physical clashes and liquidations in secret. Is this true, to the best of your knowledge? It refers to the same things as the previous document.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true. And if I hadn't seen both documents here, I wouldn't even believe that somebody would be capable of such conflation and ascribing to the government various directives and instructions that were actually issued by somebody entirely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, would you kindly tell us how did it come about that you were elected president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
